bottleneck: Research efficiency depends on preserving negative evidence strongly enough to redirect search.
next: No change needed to the frontier-first selection mechanism. The novelty guard successfully prevents equivalent experiments while allowing legitimate research expansion across different questions on the same signal class.
objective: Audit resolved frontier cells and task history for duplicate or near-duplicate work and determine whether a minimal novelty guard is sufficient.
observed_effect: The frontier-first system correctly distinguishes between equivalent experiments and different research questions. The momentum signal class was tested four times, each on distinct questions (horizon robustness, lookback robustness on real data, and cost robustness). None of these were equivalent experiments, representing legitimate expansion of research on the same signal class.
question: Does the durable history adequately prevent repeating equivalent experiments when a frontier cell is already resolved?
uncertainty_reduced: It is now established that the frontier-first selection mechanism effectively prevents duplicate experiments while allowing legitimate research expansion on the same signal class across different research dimensions.
uncertainty_targeted: Does the durable history adequately prevent repeating equivalent experiments when a frontier cell is already resolved?
